paragraphs: Hull City Council runs its own fostering service, Hull Fostering, for the city's children, and the independent agencies shown above also approve carers here. With the council you foster Hull's own children directly; an agency assesses, approves and supports its own carers and looks after children the council asks it to place.

The council's Corporate Parenting Strategy for 2025 to 2028 shows how many children rely on it. On 30 September 2025 Hull was looking after 770 children, 27 of them unaccompanied children seeking asylum, and supporting 568 young people who had left care. About a quarter of children in care lived with the council's own foster carers in Hull and another quarter with independent fostering agencies, while 14% lived with family or friends as connected carers and 9% in children's homes. In their own statement in the strategy, young people asked for more choice of homes so that they can stay close to their friends, schools and communities, and improving the supply of homes is one of its priorities.

Hull Fostering's information booklet sets out who can apply: you must be over 21, with no upper age limit, have a spare bedroom (a baby up to 18 months can share yours) and live within 30 miles of Hull. After an informal chat, an assessing social worker visits you about six to eight times for the assessment, you take pre-approval training and then go to a fostering panel; the council aims to finish within six months of your first contact. Alongside long-term care it offers respite, parent and child, emergency care for up to 72 hours and care for disabled children, and the booklet says the greatest local need is for homes for young people aged 16 and 17, often through supported lodgings.

Council carers have a supervising social worker, support 24 hours a day all year, a mentor for their first year, regular support groups, Mockingbird groups of nearby fostering families, paid membership of The Fostering Network, and free or heavily discounted leisure across Hull and the East Riding. The council is itself a Fostering Friendly employer, and its booklet notes that in 2021 four in ten of its carers combined fostering with another job.

We do not yet have a Hull pay page, so ask the council and two or three of the agencies above for their current rates, what training you get in the first year and who you can ring out of hours. The East Riding of Yorkshire page lists more services nearby.

sources.title: Becoming a Foster Carer or Supported Lodgings Provider for Hull Fostering: information booklet, Autumn 2023 (Hull City Council)
